caption: The drawing depicts an overhead view of a formal garden layout. At the center is a large, symmetrical, rectangular building in shades of gray and purple, surrounded by several geometric paths and structures in white and green. There are two statues of animals at the base of a staircase leading away from the building. To the sides and behind the building are various rectangular garden plots, some with grids and others filled with green, white, and other light colors, indicating different types of vegetation or cultivation. Curved and straight walking paths, composed of tan and white, wind through dark green grassy areas and patches of trees rendered with green canopies. At the uppermost edge, a rectangular plot with white patches appears to represent a pergola or arbor area, bordered by a semicircle of trees. Toward the lower part of the image, there are several symmetrical parterre gardens filled with red, yellow, purple, and green, arranged within outlined beds. The bottom left shows a dark green tennis court marked with white lines. A striped circular area in red and white is located just left of center. Light tan walkways link all sections, and smaller dots and rounded shapes represent trees and shrubs. The entire composition is balanced along a vertical axis, with the label "THE GARDEN OF THOMAS G. VEITCH" and "THE BLACKWELL SURVEY" along the bottom border.
title: Thomas C. Veitch Estate
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
